Spec notes (from the token source)

Buttons. One filled primary per view region (a page, a dialog, a panel; the floating layer is its own region). Labels are sentence case, --type-button 14/20 600, never multi-line (white-space: nowrap). Loading keeps width and label and appends the text dots (no spinner). Success for idempotent actions is a 2 s label swap with the check icon; for submits it is a toast. A tertiary button used as a toggle (aria-pressed) draws its pressed state as the selection tint + --selection-text + a 2 px --selection-marker bar (the tertiary pressed variant); primary and secondary buttons are never toggles. Keyboard: Tab reaches each button, Enter and Space press; a loading button stays in the tab order (aria-busy) and ignores presses.

primary · default
Filled.
primary · hover
Fill steps to --accent-solid-hover, instantly.
primary · focus
:focus-visible 2 px --focus-ring at 2 px offset.
primary · active
Pressed: the fill steps past hover to --accent-solid-active (light: the system's green-black; dark: accent-12) with scale 0.98 for 150 ms, so pressed is told from hovered by fill, not by the scale alone.
primary · disabled
Disabled: --disabled-surface fill, --disabled-text label, --disabled-border hairline; the reason is stated in adjacent helper text, or in a toggletip on the control itself, which stays focusable (aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled attribute) and opens it on hover, focus and tap, showing the text inline under (hover: none); either way it is linked by aria-describedby so keyboard and touch users read it too. Never a bare grey control.
primary · loading
aria-busy; label stays, trailing text dots cycle (3 frames, 500 ms) in a fixed 3ch slot; width fixed; the control is disabled while busy.
primary · error
The button returns to default; the failure is an adjacent inline alert (role=alert) which receives focus. The button itself is never recoloured.
primary · success
Idempotent actions (Copy): label swaps to the past tense with the check icon for 2 s, then reverts. Submits: a success toast; the button returns to default.
secondary · default
Outlined: --surface fill, --border-interactive boundary, --accent-text label.
secondary · hover
Tint hover.
secondary · focus
Ring; the boundary does not change colour.
secondary · active
Pressed: the tint steps to --accent-bg-subtle-active (accent-4, past the accent-3 hover) + scale 0.98.
secondary · disabled
Disabled: --disabled-surface fill, --disabled-text label, --disabled-border hairline; the reason is stated in adjacent helper text, or in a toggletip on the control itself, which stays focusable (aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled attribute) and opens it on hover, focus and tap, showing the text inline under (hover: none); either way it is linked by aria-describedby so keyboard and touch users read it too. Never a bare grey control.
secondary · loading
As primary loading.
secondary · error
As primary error (adjacent alert).
secondary · success
As primary success.
tertiary · default
Text only on a transparent fill; --accent-text label.
tertiary · hover
Tint hover: --accent-bg-subtle behind the label.
tertiary · focus
Ring on the transparent control.
tertiary · active
Pressed: the tint steps to --accent-bg-subtle-active (accent-4, past the accent-3 hover) + scale 0.98.
tertiary · disabled
Disabled tertiary: there is no fill to grey, so the label drops to --disabled-text at weight 400 (enabled tertiary labels are 600) and the reason sits beside it in helper text or a toggletip on the control itself (aria-disabled, aria-describedby; shown inline under (hover: none)). Disabled is told apart by weight and the stated reason, never by hue alone.
tertiary · loading
As primary loading.
tertiary · error
As primary error.
tertiary · success
As primary success.
destructive · default
Outlined: --destructive-text boundary and label on --surface; trash icon optional.
destructive · hover
Tint hover: --destructive-bg-subtle; label and boundary unchanged.
destructive · focus
The standard --focus-ring: one focus signal system-wide.
destructive · active
Pressed: the error-3 tint (the functional ramp has no fourth step) + scale 0.98; the hue, icon and label already set it apart.
destructive · disabled
Disabled: --disabled-surface fill, --disabled-text label, --disabled-border hairline; the reason is stated in adjacent helper text, or in a toggletip on the control itself, which stays focusable (aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled attribute) and opens it on hover, focus and tap, showing the text inline under (hover: none); either way it is linked by aria-describedby so keyboard and touch users read it too. Never a bare grey control. A destructive button is disabled while nothing is selected ("Select students to remove").
destructive · loading
Label + dots; the dialog's other controls disable; close stays enabled unless the request cannot be cancelled.
destructive · error
Returns to default; the failure is an inline error alert above the actions.
destructive · success
The dialog closes; a toast confirms with the count ("3 students removed") and, where reversible, Undo beside Dismiss; the toast is the next tab stop after the trigger and stays until dismissed (or at least 10 s, paused on hover, focus-within and window blur), so the undo is reachable by keyboard.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Icon-only buttons (chat header, top bar, feedback toolbar, row actions). Neutral: --icon-default glyph on a transparent fill; hover/pressed tint tonally; a selected icon button (the current chat mode, TD-09; aria-pressed="true") is the selection tint + --accent-text glyph + a 2 px --selection-marker bar along its bottom edge, never a purple icon and never colour alone. Every icon button has an aria-label and a tooltip; a disabled one keeps focus (aria-disabled) and carries its reason in a toggletip on the control itself (hover, focus and tap; inline helper under (hover: none)), wired with aria-describedby ("Not available yet"). Keyboard: as buttons; a toggled icon button exposes aria-pressed; inside a toolbar it joins the toolbar's roving tabindex.

Neutral glyph (--icon-default) on a transparent fill.
hover
Tonal fill (--surface-hover); the glyph darkens to --icon-hover.
focus
Ring.
active
Pressed: tonal + scale 0.98.
disabled
Disabled icon: --disabled-icon (border-strong); the reason opens as a toggletip on hover, focus and tap and is read with the control (Regenerate, Share: "Not available yet").
loading
The glyph is replaced by the static dashed ring in --in-progress-text, aria-busy and inert; the progress is stated in adjacent text that the control is described by ("Copying…", G9).
error
The glyph swaps to the cross in --status-error-text for 2 s with the tooltip / aria-live text saying what failed.

The glyph swaps to the check in --status-success-text for 2 s with the label ("Copied"); then reverts.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Chips. Three kinds with one colour rule each (TD-35, TD-40): status chips are the only tinted chips (-3 surface, -11 icon + label); filter chips are controls (--border-interactive boundary; selected = selection tint + --accent-text 600); role chips are labels (--surface-active, --text, no border). A row never carries two saturated fills. Keyboard: filter chips are toggle buttons (one tab stop each, Space or Enter toggles, aria-pressed); status and role chips are not in the tab order.

status · default
The status variant that applies (info shown).
status · hover
No change: not interactive.
status · focus
Not focusable; no ring.
status · active
None: not pressable.
status · disabled
Never disabled: a status is a fact, not a control.
status · loading
The neutral variant with the ring icon and dots ("Importing…").
status · error
The error variant (cross + label).
status · success
The success variant (check + label).
filter · default
Unselected: --border-interactive boundary, --text label, --surface fill (aria-pressed=false).

Tonal fill.

Ring.

Pressed.
filter · disabled
Disabled: --disabled-surface fill, --disabled-text label, --disabled-border hairline; the reason is stated in adjacent helper text, or in a toggletip on the control itself, which stays focusable (aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled attribute) and opens it on hover, focus and tap, showing the text inline under (hover: none); either way it is linked by aria-describedby so keyboard and touch users read it too. Never a bare grey control. ("No recitations in this class").
filter · loading
While a filter applies asynchronously: the ring icon replaces the count; aria-busy.
filter · error
Filters do not fail in place; a failed query is a toast and the chip returns to default.

None: applying a filter is its own feedback (the list changes).

Spec notes (from the token source)

Switch: a selection control (D4, TD-22). Off = --surface track, --border-interactive boundary and thumb; On = selection tint track, --accent-text boundary and thumb. Status green never styles a switch. Thumb travel 150 ms with --easing-toggle; colours switch instantly. Label always visible; a saving switch shows the ring icon beside its label. Keyboard: Tab to the switch, Space toggles (role=switch, aria-checked); the visible label is the accessible name. Shape: track and thumb are rectangles at --radius-control (2 px): the lock reserves --radius-round for status dots and the mascot's backing circle and allows no pill, so the switch reads as a slider, never as an oval.

default
Off.
hover
Track tints tonally; thumb darkens to --text.
focus
Ring around the track.
active
Pressed: the thumb starts its travel.
disabled
Disabled: --disabled-surface fill, --disabled-text label, --disabled-border hairline; the reason is stated in adjacent helper text, or in a toggletip on the control itself, which stays focusable (aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled attribute) and opens it on hover, focus and tap, showing the text inline under (hover: none); either way it is linked by aria-describedby so keyboard and touch users read it too. Never a bare grey control. ("Only admins can change this").
loading
Saving: the thumb already sits in the requested position, the ring icon beside the label and aria-busy say the change is pending, and the control is inert until the server answers. The boundary stays --border-interactive (a busy control is still a control, not a disabled one).
error
The thumb reverts to the previous position; an inline helper (cross + what failed + how to retry) appears under the label.
success
The position holds; a success helper (check + label) appears only when the change needed a server round trip, for 2 s.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Text inputs, selects and textareas (one family). Visible label above (--type-label), control at --size-control with the --border-interactive boundary, helper text below (--type-caption). Placeholder is a format hint, never the label. Validate on blur, re-validate on keystroke after the first error; errors say what happened, why, how to fix (Phase 5 words). Selects keep 40 px right padding so the chevron clears the value (TD-13). Textareas: min 3 rows, resize vertical. Checkboxes and radios are their own component (§ Checkboxes and radios). Keyboard: Tab in document order; a select opens with Enter, Space or Down and closes with Escape.

default
Resting: label above, --border-interactive boundary, placeholder as a format hint, helper below.
hover
Boundary darkens to --text.
focus
The ring is the only focus signal; the boundary does not change colour.
active
Typing is the focus state; no separate pressed look.
disabled
Disabled: --disabled-surface fill, --disabled-text label, --disabled-border hairline; the reason is stated in adjacent helper text, or in a toggletip on the control itself, which stays focusable (aria-disabled="true", never the native disabled attribute) and opens it on hover, focus and tap, showing the text inline under (hover: none); either way it is linked by aria-describedby so keyboard and touch users read it too. Never a bare grey control. ("Set by your institution").
loading
Async validation or options loading: trailing "Loading…" text in --in-progress-text with the ring icon; the control stays editable unless options are required.
error
aria-invalid; boundary --status-error-text; helper = cross icon + message, linked by aria-describedby.
success
Only for server-confirmed values ("Email available"): helper = check icon + message; the boundary stays neutral.

Checkboxes and radios

Checkboxes and radios: selection controls (D4), one family with one colour rule.

light

comfortable

compact

Spec notes (from the token source)

Checkboxes and radios: selection controls (D4), one family with one colour rule. An 18 px box (a radio: the same box with --radius-round and an 8 px dot) at --checkbox-size with the --border-interactive boundary on --surface; checked and indeterminate = the selection tint fill with the --selection-text glyph (the check, the dash, the dot), so the state is a shape change, never the hue alone; the label (--type-label at weight 400) is the accessible name and is clickable; a group has a group label and one helper line. A row checkbox in a table or DataGrid has no visible label, so its name is aria-label="Select {the row's first text cell}" ("Select Lin Yue"); the header checkbox is "Select all rows" and shows the dash (aria-checked="mixed") while some rows are selected. Keyboard: a checkbox is one tab stop and Space toggles it (aria-checked true / false / mixed); a radio group is one tab stop and Up/Down or Left/Right move the selection; a disabled box stays focusable (aria-disabled) with its reason in a toggletip and the helper.

default
Unchecked (a radio: unselected): --surface fill, --border-interactive boundary, no glyph; the label in --text at weight 400.
hover
The boundary darkens to --text (as a field's does); the fill does not change.
focus
The ring around the box (2 px --focus-ring at 2 px offset); the boundary does not change.
active
Pressed: --surface-active fill with the --text boundary (the glyph appears on release).
disabled
Disabled: the disabled trio (--disabled-surface fill, --disabled-border boundary, a --disabled-icon glyph if checked) and the label in --disabled-text at weight 400, with the reason stated in the group's helper or the row's reason and linked by aria-describedby; the box stays focusable (aria-disabled); a row that cannot be acted on disables its checkbox this way ("Professors are removed by an admin").
loading
Saving a change that needs the server (a per-row permission): the box is inert (aria-busy) and keeps the requested state, the label gains the text dots ("Saving…"), and the ring icon sits beside it; the boundary stays --border-interactive.
error
A required box left unchecked at submit, or a group that failed to save: aria-invalid, the boundary --status-error-text, the cross icon + what happened and how to fix under the group (aria-describedby); the fill does not change.
success
Only for a server-confirmed change: the box checked (the checked variant) with a check + "Saved" helper for 2 s.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Tabs (class tabs, admin page tabs, the IDE output tabs). --type-label 14/20 600 for every tab so selection does not reflow; unselected --text-secondary, selected --accent-text with a 2 px --selection-marker underline. Height per density. On overflow the list scrolls behind its own edges with chevron scroll buttons at the ends (MUI variant="scrollable", scrollButtons="auto", --icon-default) and no edge fade (the lock permits gradients only as hard stops); never wraps. Keyboard: the tab list is one tab stop with a roving tabindex: Left/Right move and select (automatic activation, MUI's default), Home/End jump to the first and last tab, Tab leaves to the panel; a disabled tab stays reachable by the arrows (aria-disabled) so its reason toggletip opens on focus, and Enter or Space do nothing on it.

default
Unselected.
hover
Tonal fill; the label darkens to --text.
focus
Ring inset −2 px (the tab bar clips).
active
Pressed.
disabled
Disabled tab: the label stays legible in --disabled-text (≥ 4.5) and drops to weight 400 (every other tab label is 600); the reason ("No plots yet") is a toggletip that opens on hover, focus and tap, so the tab stays reachable by the arrow keys (aria-disabled, kept in the roving order) and cannot be activated.
loading
The tab is unchanged; its panel shows a skeleton.
error
A tab whose panel failed shows the 16 px cross icon in --status-error-text after its label with a visually hidden "failed to load" for assistive tech: a shape and words, never colour alone (G1); the panel holds the error alert.
success
None: tabs are navigation.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Panels: a --surface sheet on the --background canvas, 1 px --border hairline, --radius-sheet, padding --space-panel. Sections inside are separated by --border-subtle rules and space, never by another panel (no nested cards). A control's --border-interactive boundary inside a panel is a signifier, not a container. Docked panels cast no shadow. Keyboard: a scrollable region is focusable (tabindex=0) and scrolls with the arrow keys; otherwise a panel has no keyboard behaviour of its own.

A --surface sheet with a --border hairline on the canvas; sections divided by --border-subtle rules.
hover
None: panels are not interactive.
focus
Only a keyboard-scrollable overflow region (tabindex=0) shows the ring, inset −2 px.
active
None.
disabled
Never: a panel's controls disable individually; the panel never greys.
loading
A skeleton of its content shape inside (shimmer permitted); the frame and title stay.
error
An inline error alert at the top of the panel (role=alert); the panel itself is not recoloured.

An inline status (check + label) or a toast; no panel-level change.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Dialogs: a --surface sheet with --shadow-2, 1 px --border, --radius-sheet, over the --backdrop (shadow-ink at 40 / 60 %). Width min(100% - 2 * var(--space-popup-margin), var(--dialog-width-sm|md|lg)) with height ≤ 80vh and a scrolling body, so a phone keeps a 12 px margin around it. Title --type-section-title, body at the page's density, body measure ≤ 75ch. Actions right-aligned: one filled primary (or the outlined destructive for confirmations) and a tertiary Cancel. Focus moves to the first focusable element, the background is inert, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger. Enter: fade + 8 px translate, 220 ms; exit 176 ms. Keyboard: on open focus moves to the first focusable element (the title for confirmations), Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger; the background is inert.

Open.
hover
None on the sheet; its controls hover.
focus

None.
disabled

The primary shows label + dots; the other controls disable; close stays enabled unless the request cannot be cancelled.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Alerts: the -3 surface with the -11 shape icon and text (check / triangle / cross / i); no coloured left border; --radius-control; padding 12/16. Title 600 + body. An optional action (Retry, Dismiss, Change range) is a text action in the status's -11 colour: underlined at rest (1 px, --border-width-underline), 600; hover thickens the underline to 2 px; focus is the ring; pressed is the 2 px underline with the shared press scale. The same pattern draws the toast's and the banner's actions, so a text action looks one way everywhere and its affordance does not depend on hover. The neutral variant is the in-progress notice (ring icon + dots). Keyboard: Tab reaches the text action and the dismiss button (the action is a link-styled button, so Enter and Space press it); an alert that appears after a failed submit (role=alert) receives focus.

default
The variant that applies (info shown); its text action underlined at rest (1 px).
hover
The hovered action's underline thickens to 2 px; the surface does not change.
focus
The ring on the focused action or dismiss button; an error alert with role=alert receives focus when it appears after a failed submit.
active
Pressed action: the 2 px underline and the shared press scale (0.98 for --motion-micro).
disabled
Never: an alert is a message.
loading
The neutral variant: ring icon, dots, and the neutral LinearProgress (--in-progress-bar on --in-progress-track).

The error variant: what happened, why, how to fix; a Retry action where one exists.

Toasts

Toasts (snackbars): a --surface sheet with --shadow-1 and a 1 px --border, max 420 px, entering from the bottom edge by 8 px in 220 ms.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Toasts (snackbars): a --surface sheet with --shadow-1 and a 1 px --border, max 420 px, entering from the bottom edge by 8 px in 220 ms. Neutral text, or a status icon + label in the status's -11. Bottom-right 24/16 px measured from the safe area (bottom: calc(var(--toast-offset-y) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); bottom-left on app tabs, beside the launcher); one at a time. Timing (WCAG 2.2.1): an info or success toast without an action auto-dismisses after 6 s, and its timer pauses while the pointer is over it, while anything inside it has focus (focus-within) and while the window has lost focus; a toast that carries an action (Undo after a removal) stays until dismissed, or at least 10 s under the same pause rules; error toasts persist until dismissed. Every toast carries Dismiss; an error toast adds Retry where a retry exists; an Undo toast shows Undo beside Dismiss. Keyboard path: the toast is rendered immediately after the control that raised it, so it is the next tab stop (one Tab from the trigger reaches Undo or Dismiss, Shift+Tab returns); the live region announces the message, and an error toast (role=alert) takes focus while an info or success toast (role=status) does not; Escape dismisses the focused toast. Queue: a new info or success toast replaces a visible info or success toast that carries no action; a toast with an action and an error toast are never replaced silently: they stay until dismissed and later toasts queue behind them (first in, first out, at most three queued; identical messages collapse into one with a count).

default
Neutral / info message: the i glyph in --icon-default (the toast's icon.default role), the text, and Dismiss as an underlined text action in --link (the one text-action pattern); 6 s unless paused.
hover
The auto-dismiss timer pauses (as it does on focus-within and on window blur); a hovered action thickens its underline to 2 px; the sheet itself does not change.
focus
Ring on Dismiss / the action. The toast is the next tab stop after the control that raised it; an error toast (role=alert) takes focus, an info or success toast (role=status) does not; Escape dismisses the focused toast.
active
Pressed action: the 2 px underline and the shared press scale.
disabled
Never.
loading
In progress ("Exporting…"): ring icon + dots, no auto-dismiss, replaced by the outcome.
error
Persistent until dismissed: cross + what failed, Retry where a retry exists and Dismiss always; later toasts queue behind it.
success
Check + label ("3 students enrolled") with Dismiss, 6 s unless hovered, focused or the window loses focus; a success toast that carries Undo (after a removal) stays until dismissed or at least 10 s under the same pause rules and is never replaced by a later toast.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Tables sit on the canvas as rules, not cards: outer --border rules top and bottom, --border-subtle row dividers, no fill. Header --type-label in --text-secondary; cells --type-body (compact 14/20); numbers right-aligned with tabular numerals; dates fixed-format. Cells are one line with ellipsis and the full text in a tooltip on hover and focus (the truncated span is focusable), except designated wrap columns clamped at two lines. Minimum column widths; below their sum the table scrolls in its own container, never the page. Toolbar buttons never wrap: below a 1120 px container they collapse to icon + count. In the toolbar the destructive action (Remove selected) is left-aligned at the start, a flexible spacer away from Email selected and the filled primary at the end, in the labelled and the collapsed variant alike (placed apart, D4). Selected rows: selection tint + 2 px inset marker. Keyboard: Tab moves between the focusable cells (links, truncated spans, row checkboxes) in reading order; Space toggles a row's checkbox; sortable headers are buttons.

default
Rows on the canvas (or on a panel sheet).
hover
Row hover: --surface-hover, instantly.
focus
Ring inset −2 px on the focused row, cell or truncated span.
active
Pressed row (selectable tables).
disabled
A row that cannot be acted on: --disabled-text with the reason in a toggletip (hover, focus and tap; inline under (hover: none), aria-describedby) ("Professors are removed by an admin"); its checkbox is disabled.

The empty-state frame

The empty-state frame (no classes, no conversation yet, no experiments, no results, not found): on the ruled reading column; the mascot still pose in the companion.slot.empty slot (Phase 4 sizes it; this phase fixes the surround: 24 px below the slot, 8 px between line and copy); a --type-page-title line (--type-display-lg for page-level empties); copy in --text-secondary at --type-body; at most one primary button. No illustration beyond the mascot, no card, no gradient. Never shown while loading (the skeleton holds the slot). Keyboard: the call to action is the frame's one tab stop; Enter or Space presses it. A role without the action (a student with no classes yet, an instructor without the create-class permission) sees no call to action at all: the no-action variant, hidden, never disabled (JOURNEY D-4). The disabled state is reserved for a role that has the action while a precondition is unmet, with the precondition stated in the copy.

Spec notes (from the token source)

The tutor-message surface: a tutor row is a 32 px avatar slot (G9) + 12 px gap + the answer column, on the message region's ruler (text 68 px right of the rule). Answer text --type-body 16/24, CJK-dominant blocks 28, measure 68ch, blocks 12 px apart, messages 24 px apart. Links --link underlined. Code blocks: --type-code 14/24 on a transparent ground with a 2 px --editor-block-rule left rule and a Copy icon button (--tutor-message-copy-button 28 px with a 16 px glyph; hit area --tutor-message-copy-hit: 28 fine / 44 coarse); inline code on --editor-inline-bg; display math bare and centred with overflow scroll. Citations [Page N] are --link in --type-caption with a 44 px hit area on coarse pointers (--tutor-message-citation-hit). The feedback toolbar is a row of 28 px icon buttons (16 px glyphs, 44 px targets on coarse pointers) on a 28 px line so it ticks once; the two thumbs are toggles (aria-pressed) and the chosen one is drawn as a filled glyph in --selection-text, the other as an outline. The panel's chrome (header, session bar, model select, composer) is compact tool chrome on every route, student pages included (36 px icon buttons and a 36 px composer field and Send), while the message region is a comfortable reading surface (16/24); on coarse pointers the chrome's controls carry 44 px hit areas. While an answer streams the composer's Send becomes Stop (secondary) and the toolbar is hidden until the answer completes. Keyboard: the feedback toolbar is one tab stop with a roving tabindex (Left/Right between its five buttons, Enter or Space presses); citations are links; the Copy button is a tab stop inside its code block; Escape while the composer has focus stops a streaming answer.

default
A complete answer on the panel sheet; the companion is idle (Phase 4).
hover
Only the toolbar buttons and citations hover (icon-button rules); text never does.
focus
Ring on toolbar buttons, citations and the Copy button.
active
Pressed toolbar button.
disabled
Regenerate and Share: --disabled-icon glyphs with the reason "Not available yet" in a toggletip on the control itself (aria-disabled keeps it focusable; hover, focus and tap; inline under (hover: none)), wired with aria-describedby (SF-53); never a silent grey.
loading
Waiting: the text dots in --in-progress-text where the answer will start ("Thinking…" + dots, Phase 5 words) and the companion walks (Phase 4); the composer is disabled with its own stated reason ("Kiwi is answering; Stop interrupts", aria-describedby) and Send becomes Stop (secondary), which stays enabled. Streaming: text appears as it arrives, unanimated; Stop stays; the toolbar is hidden.
error
An error row: cross icon + what happened and how to retry in --status-error-text on the --status-error-surface, with a Retry secondary button (not filled); the companion shows its error pose.
success
Answer complete: the toolbar appears enabled, the composer re-enables and takes focus; the chosen thumb is drawn filled in --selection-text (aria-pressed="true") and the other stays an outline in --icon-default (today both grey out); the companion hops once (Phase 4).

Spec notes (from the token source)

The PDF viewer (react-pdf): the toolbar and the surfaces around the paper, on S-02 (file name, previous / next, "n / N", zoom out, "100 %", zoom in, fullscreen), S-09 and A-24 (Search and Thumbnails as tertiary toggles whose pressed look is the tertiary pressed variant (aria-pressed), First, Previous, the page field "3 / 12", Next, Last, zoom, Fit width, Open / print, Fullscreen; the search panel; the thumbnail strip). The bar is tool chrome on both areas: 44 px, on --surface with a 1 px --border-subtle bottom rule, holding compact (36 px) icon buttons with --icon-default glyphs, the file name in --type-label, page and zoom labels in --type-caption tabular --text-secondary, 1 px × 18 px --border-subtle dividers, and the page field as a compact field (--border-interactive). The scroll area is the canvas (--background) with --space-panel padding; each page is paper on a 1 px --paper-frame hairline (no shadow: docked surfaces cast none), dimmed to 92 % in dark mode (--pdf-toolbar-paper-dim → --opacity-paper-dim) so the white paper does not glare; the page the chat has in context carries a 2 px --border-interactive outline and the bar shows the neutral "In context" chip, so the cue is not colour alone and no brand colour touches the paper's edge (TD-08). Marks drawn on the paper never follow the mode (G5): comment pins visible to students are --on-paper-pin discs with the 16 px speech-bubble glyph in --on-paper-page (the system's own SVG: an emoji ignores color, has no token and varies by platform); hidden-from-students pins (A-24) are --on-paper-page discs with a 2 px --on-paper-pin ring; chunk boxes are 1 px --on-paper-chunk, the selected chunk 2 px --on-paper-pin over the --on-paper-wash, the drag box dashed --on-paper-chunk. The search panel is a floating --surface sheet (1 px --border, --shadow-1) with a compact field, Find (secondary) and Next match (tertiary) and a status line; the thumbnail strip shows paper miniatures on hairline frames on the canvas, the current one outlined like the page, with --type-caption page numbers. The summary banner is an info alert (--status-info-surface, the i glyph and text in --status-info-text, Read as its action, an icon-button close) floating at the top of the viewer with --shadow-1; its re-show button is a neutral icon button with the neutral count badge. The student page's icon rail and "Class Materials" drawer are a panel with sidebar-item rows (the selected file: selection tint + check glyph) and two exclusive filter chips (Lecture / Recitation). Keyboard: the toolbar is one tab stop with a roving tabindex (Left/Right move between its buttons, Enter/Space press; the page field takes digits and Enter); Escape closes the search panel and returns focus to Search.

Only the control whose boundary is reached is disabled, each with its own reason as a toggletip and in the bar's helper line: Previous and First on page 1 ("You're on the first page"), Next and Last on the last page, Zoom out or Zoom in at the zoom clamp ("Smallest zoom"); every other button stays enabled, so today's silent clamp becomes a stated boundary.

Spec notes (from the token source)

The third axis. Touch devices (student routes on phones, G13) get 44 × 44 px hit areas without changing the drawn size: the emitted token CSS carries an @media (pointer: coarse) block that re-points the hit and pitch roles to --size-target-min in every density block, and each control extends its hit area with a pseudo-element sized to the hit token and centred on the control (so a border never shrinks it): icon buttons, the feedback toolbar and the code block's Copy button, filter chips, switches, checkboxes and radios, menu items, the PDF bar's buttons, the text actions and citations, the S-02 drawer's file rows and the comment pins on the paper. The feedback toolbar's five 28 px buttons move from a 30 px to a 44 px pitch (5 × 44 = 220 px fits the 420 px panel and a 390 px phone) while the glyphs stay on the 28 px line; the drawer's 36 px rows open to a 44 px pitch the same way. The stated exceptions are the admin-only sidebar rows and the admin tables' compact rows with their checkboxes (desktop chrome; 36 px clears WCAG 2.5.8's 24 px); every other control on a student route reaches 44 px: links inside running prose fall under WCAG 2.5.8's inline exception (the citations are not prose links and carry their own hit areas), the admin tables' name-link cells join the admin-only exceptions, and the comfortable 44 px controls need no extension. Headless desktop Chrome reports a fine pointer, so the coarse exhibits re-declare the emitted media block under .emu-coarse (the same declarations); the dashed outlines draw the hit areas; DESIGN.md's evidence also records a hit test under real (pointer: coarse) emulation over the DevTools protocol.

Forced colours (@media (forced-colors: active))

Windows High Contrast and other forced-colours modes replace the author colours with the system palette and drop box-shadow, so a marker drawn as an inset shadow (the selected icon button, the pressed tertiary toggle, the selected tab, the current sidebar row, the selected table row) would vanish and a selected control would look like a resting one.

dark

Spec notes (from the token source)

Windows High Contrast and other forced-colours modes replace the author colours with the system palette and drop box-shadow, so a marker drawn as an inset shadow (the selected icon button, the pressed tertiary toggle, the selected tab, the current sidebar row, the selected table row) would vanish and a selected control would look like a resting one. The component CSS carries an @media (forced-colors: active) block that redraws each marker as a 2 px Highlight outline (outline-offset −2 px), gives the dots and the dash (backgrounds, which forced colours erase) a CanvasText fill and the switch thumb a CanvasText border, and leaves the cues that survive as system colours (the check and filled glyphs, the chip's weight 600, the thumb's position) as they are. The paper and the marks on it are content, not chrome (forced-color-adjust: none, as react-pdf's rendered bitmap would be), so the pins keep their fixed G5 colours and the hidden pin its ring: forced colours do not recolour an SVG glyph, so a white glyph on a Canvas-forced disc would otherwise vanish. The exhibit emulates the one property that matters (box-shadow: none under .emu-forced) and applies the same declarations; the audit counts every selected, pressed, current or checked control inside it and fails one without a surviving cue; DESIGN.md's evidence adds a real (forced-colors: active) emulation over the DevTools protocol.

Spec notes (from the token source)

Code editors, code blocks and consoles follow the mode; they are not paper (G5). One role set drives the Ace themes, the Prism style object and the console. The editable editor is a control (its host carries --editor-border-editable); read-only viewers and the console are sheets with the --editor-border hairline. Low-chroma, weight-led syntax roles (D7): keywords by weight, strings in the accent, numbers in info, diagnostics in error/warning. Two hues in code so status stays status. The Ace themes, the Prism style object and the console CSS are generated from the same roles by build-tokens.mjs (generated/code-themes/).

Audit (measured on load) and reading notes

Audit: measuring…

The first style block is the generated token CSS; each exhibit takes its colours from the component tier through [data-c][data-v][data-s] rules generated from the same DTCG source, and its geometry from the density-aware size and space roles, so what you see is what the tokens say. Every disabled or inert control states its reason (helper text or a toggletip, wired with aria-describedby) and is WCAG-exempt only for its own contrast; every control nested inside another component is checked against its canonical exhibit.

What to confirm by eye: one filled control per region; the destructive action is outlined, never red-filled; switches and checkboxes tint when on rather than fill; status chips are the only tinted chips; text actions in alerts, toasts and the banner are underlined and drawn one way; table figures are ink, not blue; compact controls are 36 px and comfortable 44 px with the same type scale; the dark column stays warm and the sage filled control reads as the one button; every focus ring is the same 2 px ring; nothing is a card inside a card; nothing truncates in the tables.

Tokens: .design-foundations/tokens/kiwi-ui.tokens.json → build-tokens.mjs → the first style block of this page. Checks: check-tokens.mjs (alias equality against the locked block, the per-state contrast assertions, the tier rule, the deprecation schedule, the per-mode, per-density and coarse-pointer closure of the emitted CSS, the public mapping). Mascot artwork: kiwi-ui/public/favicon.svg, exact colours (G11); its states, poses and slot sizes are Phase 4. Montserrat appears nowhere on this sheet.
